text.p: Italian debt markets ended with sturdy gains as technical factors and in some cases shortcovering drove them higher, traders said.
A strong lira, at its highest levels against the mark since mid-June 1994 at 974.95 per mark, also lent the debt market a helping hand, dealers said.

One trader at an Italian bank in London said the March Btp had tested the bottom of its range just below 127.00 earlier in the week, failed to break it and was now trying out the top end, causing short covering. The March future was 77 basis points higher at 128.81 with immediate support at 128.55 and 128.20.
Resistance for the future was seen by some as 128.86, the top of the range, and by others as 128.95. Beyond that, 129.40/55 was cited.

A senior government official said Italy may need a supplementary budget to plug its 1996 deficit overshoot and it could be drawn up sooner than expected -- without necessarily waiting for the country's quarterly accounts, which traders said gave Italian markets a boost. Quarterly accounts are usually published around March.
For tomorrow the market will be waiting for U.S. non-farm payrolls data before it makes much of a move, dealers said.

At home, investors are still waiting for resolution of a bitter dispute between engineering unions and employers over pay, with a solution expected to prompt a cut in official interest rates by the Bank of Italy. However, for now the talks remain deadlocked.
